passage: Diary, Friday. Pema. Went to the music night with Varun. When the band started their old hit the entire hall whooped and screamed and I joined in, arms up, voice cracking, and it felt amazing, like we were all one big animal. Then on Sunday Varun dragged me to a classical recital and I whooped by mistake after the flute solo. Nobody else made a sound. Heads turned. My face went hot. Varun whispered that people there clap quietly. I laughed at myself. Both places are fun, just differently. Next time I'll watch what the room does first. I still think loud joy is a good thing when everyone is in on it. 🙂

qa.q: Who went to the music night with Pema?
What was Pema feeling after whooping in the recital?
qa.a: Pema was embarrassed, as the hot face shows, but laughed at the mistake. Pema did not mean to be rude and had simply carried the concert habit into a quiet room.

qa.q: What could Pema do at an unfamiliar event?
qa.a: Watch what the room does first and match it, saving loud cheering for places where everyone joins in.

qa.q: How might the people at the recital have felt?
qa.a: The audience may have been surprised or a little disturbed in a quiet moment, though some may have found it endearing, since the cue does not prove annoyance.

grounding: A young adult joins loud cheering at a concert, which is welcome there but odd at a quiet recital, so awareness of the venue is respect.

passage:
Nirmala: I whooped at my cousin's graduation today 🎉 and the dean gave me a look
Tenzin: haha the look or a smile?
Nirmala: hard to tell. some parents clapped politely, some cheered louder than me
Tenzin: at ours everybody cheered whenever a friend went up. it was so loud 😄
Nirmala: here it's more like a quiet hall until the end
Tenzin: so was it wrong?
Nirmala: not exactly. I was just louder than the room. next time I'll clap first and see what the crowd does
Tenzin: fair
Nirmala: I still wanted her to hear someone shout her name 🙂

qa.q: What did the dean give Nirmala?
qa.a: The dean gave Nirmala a look.

qa.q: What was Nirmala thinking about the look?
qa.a: Nirmala was unsure whether it was disapproval, because some parents clapped politely and others cheered louder. Nirmala still wanted the cousin to hear a shout of joy.

qa.q: What could Nirmala do at the next quiet ceremony?
qa.a: Clap first, see what the crowd does and cheer in a way that matches the room.
At Tenzin's graduation everybody cheered loudly whenever a friend went up, so whooping was part of the custom there.

grounding: A young adult cheers at a graduation where volume is welcome in some settings and odd in others.
